chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: From the high register to the middle register
summary: He stopped playing so high because it didn't sound pretty.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I'm glad you brought that up, because this is something that's been in the back of my mind to talk about today. When I first heard you in the Jazz At the Philharmonic, and
especially those Dial records, 'Trumpet At Tempo' and 'Thermodynamics,' you were playing way up high...
I was playing up there. I wasn't just hitting the notes up there...

Oh, no, you were playing. You weren't just hitting high notes. But later, you became more of a middle-range type of trumpet player. You stopped playing a lot of your solos up high. What made you change?

Well, I didn't think that the things I was playing up high would be very pretty in the middle register. So I had to change from what I was playing upstairs; when I came back downstairs, I had to find something else to play, and to sound good, even though I wasn't playing like I used to play up high.
So that's the only thing I can figure out. I mean, it wasn't that I wanted to definitely make a definite change, except that I didn't think it was pretty, according to my ideas now.
Oh, it was exciting. Yeah, it was that. But maybe I can get back up there again. I don't know. I'll see in the next couple of weeks, see how it feels, to be able to see if I can get up the stairs.
But I remember even talking about that record you made
with Gene Ammons, which was not that long after the period where you were playing way up high. You got into a different groove, you know.
Well, with Jug it was such a groove...I mean, to be able to get into another groove, you know. But I enjoyed making the date with Jug.
